correctness.rationale: Maximum disk triangle area M=3sqrt3/4 is attained only by two oriented equilateral families. In near-maximal charts, first inward radial derivatives are c=sqrt3/2, and independent symbolic Hessian check gives B=(sqrt3/8)[[2,1],[1,2]], sqrt(det B)=3/8. Compactness localizes radial deficits O(epsilon) and relative angle defects O(sqrt(epsilon)); the Taylor remainder is uniform o(epsilon), including b in (0,1) under local regular-variation bounds. The measure Jacobian and beta integral yield C epsilon^(3b+1), C=(16pi/3) I_p a^3 c^(-3b) Gamma(b)^3/Gamma(3b+2). Polar z gives five Dirichlet shares (b,b,b,1,1); chart products give phase W/I_p, uniform angular energy phase and fair independent orientation. Independent symbolic derivatives/determinant and b=1 uniform-disk C=32/(27sqrt3 pi) passed. Finite tests cannot establish weak convergence; normal-form dominated convergence does.
